newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA-SHIPPING CO 1996 AUDITED LOSS $35.5 MLN.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-SHIPPING CO 1996 AUDITED LOSS $35.5 MLN.

text.p: Latvian Shipping Company said on Friday that its audited 1996 loss came to $35.49 million on turnover of $264.76 million, which was a decrease of 30 percent compared with 1995.
"The company's losses decreased by 30 percent in 1996," Andris Klavinsh, Latvian Shipping Company (LSC) president, told a news conference.
"Although it is not easy to get a company of this size back into the black, we hope we could perhaps start 1998 with a profit," he added.
The company, currently in its second stage of privatisation, is the world's 19th largest shipper with a fleet of 77 vessels.
It has 39 tankers, 24 refrigerated vessels, seven dry cargo ships and two gas vessels.
Klavinsh said the underlying losses of the company would be smaller at $23.7 million without one-off items which include accumulated tax debt from 1993 and 1994.
The company also made reserves of three million dollars to cover possible court damages in a ship order contract dispute with the Gdansk Shipyard in Poland.
An insurance sum of $1.3 million, which was paid out in 1993, has been included in last year's balance correcting an earlier accounting mistake, Klavinsh said.
"The underlying loss figure is in line with the $25 million mentioned earlier in the year," Krastinsh said.
"Turnover decreased from 295.06 million in 1995 but the operating profit is up six million dollars versus 1995," Klavinsh said.
The company said that the number of its employees was 800, which he said was arund the right number.
